newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Finnish Markka joins EU currency grid.
newsitem.headline: Finnish Markka joins EU currency grid.

text.p: The EU monetary committee agreed on Saturday to allow the Finnish markka to join the Exchange Rate Mechanism (ERM) currency grid at a central rate of 3.04 to the German mark, the committee said in a statement.
Entry into the ERM, which took effect immediately, is viewed as a step towards Finland joining the future EU single currency when it is launched at the start of 1999.
The markka was trading at 2.986 to the German mark at the close of business on Friday.

The statement said the markka would be allowed to fluctuate by up to 15 percent against the other currencies in the grid, the normal margins since the ERM bands were widened in August 1993 after severe pressure on the system.

After a meeting lasting more than four hours of the committee, made up of senior finance ministry and central bank officials from the 15 EU member states, the statement made no mention of other changes to the ERM, which means that Britain, Sweden, Greece and Italy remain outside the grid.

The statement said ministers, central bank governors, the (European) Commission and the European Monetary Institute "congratulated the Finnish authorities on the substantial adjustments already achieved by the Finnish economy which is reflected in this decision".
